purpose: Apply 15 code-quality and conventions fixes: structured logging, future-date validation on event creation, whyVoluntary→whyVolunteer deprecation, safer Prisma type cast, import consolidation, and denormalized User.totalHours for leaderboard performance.
riskRationale: User.totalHours is denormalized onto the User model for leaderboard performance, but no code path writes to this field — three attendance flows only update VolunteerProfile.totalHours. The leaderboard will return 0 hours for all users. No Prisma migration is included, so the new column does not exist in any database running prisma migrate deploy.
breakingChanges: User.totalHours field added to Prisma schema — requires database migration
Leaderboard now queries User.totalHours instead of joining VolunteerProfile — returns 0 hours for all existing users until backfilled

text: This PR addresses 15 code quality findings with several well-executed fixes: the logger/env.ts circular dependency is cleanly resolved, the unsafe Prisma type cast is replaced with proper TypeScript utility types, CreateEventSchema gains future-date validation, and misleading Phase 2 comments are removed. However, the totalHours denormalization is critically incomplete — User.totalHours is never populated by any attendance flow, and no Prisma migration is provided. This must be resolved before merge.

reasoning: Two critical issues block merge: (1) User.totalHours is never synced from VolunteerProfile.totalHours across all three attendance write paths — leaderboard will show 0 hours for all volunteers; (2) no Prisma migration is included for the new column and index.

message: Cleanly resolved the circular dependency between logger.ts and env.ts by switching to process.env.NODE_ENV — the correct architectural choice for a foundational utility.
Replaced unsafe `as never` cast with `Parameters<typeof prisma.$on>[0]` — a meaningful type-safety improvement using built-in TypeScript utility types.
Good separation of CreateEventSchema (with future-date validation) from EventSchema (without, for updates). Avoids forcing past-date events to be resubmitted on edit.
Backward-compatible whyVolunteer/whyVoluntary dual-field handling is well-implemented with nullish coalescing fallback.
Replaced console.error/warn with logger.error/warn, giving structured log output with timestamps and proper severity levels.
Clean removal of misleading Phase 2 comments from actively-used code.

User.totalHours is never updated. All three attendance write paths (markAttendance line 452, approveAttendance line 583, checkOut line 785) update VolunteerProfile.totalHours but not User.totalHours. The leaderboard now reads from User.totalHours, so it will always show 0 hours for every volunteer.
suggestion: Add User.totalHours updates in all three locations within the same transaction, and run a one-time data migration to copy existing VolunteerProfile.totalHours into User.totalHours for all users.

message: The new totalHours field on the User model and its compound index have no corresponding Prisma migration file. Running prisma migrate deploy will fail because the column does not exist in the database.
suggestion: Run `cd backend && npx prisma migrate dev --name add_user_total_hours` to generate a migration and include the resulting migration files in the PR.

message: Dual totalHours fields (User.totalHours and VolunteerProfile.totalHours) with no sync mechanism. The rest of the codebase (badge-engine.service.ts, levels.service.ts, stats.service.ts, etc.) still reads/writes VolunteerProfile.totalHours. Without a trigger, Prisma middleware, or shared update wrapper, these will diverge.
suggestion: Either (a) consolidate to a single source of truth and redirect all reads to User.totalHours, or (b) add a Prisma middleware that syncs User.totalHours whenever VolunteerProfile.totalHours changes, or (c) add a database trigger.

message: Existing VolunteerProfile.totalHours data is not backfilled into the new User.totalHours column. After deployment, all existing users will show 0 hours until their next attendance update.
suggestion: Add a one-time data migration (SQL script or Prisma migration with raw SQL) to copy VolunteerProfile.totalHours to User.totalHours for all existing users.

message: CreateEventSchema and EventSchema are nearly identical (only differ in eventDate validation). Deriving one from the other would reduce duplication.
suggestion: Define EventSchema using CreateEventSchema.omit({ eventDate: true }).extend({ eventDate: z.string().datetime() }) or use a shared base.

message: CreateEventSchema future-date check uses `new Date(val) > new Date()` with no tolerance. On multi-server deployments with clock skew, events created near the boundary could be incorrectly rejected.
suggestion: Add a small tolerance: `new Date(val) > new Date(Date.now() - 5000)`.

message: The endTime > startTime refinement uses lexicographic string comparison on HH:MM strings. Correct for zero-padded 24h strings but fragile if the format changes.
suggestion: Parse as minutes for robust comparison: split on ':' and compare numeric values.

message: EventSchema (used for PUT /events/:id) lacks future-date validation, so existing events can be backdated via update. Likely intentional but undocumented.
suggestion: If intentional, add a code comment. If not, add the same future-date refine from CreateEventSchema.

message: EventInput is still inferred from EventSchema rather than CreateEventSchema. Since POST now validates with CreateEventSchema, the service layer type should match.
suggestion: Add a CreateEventInput type inferred from CreateEventSchema and update createEvent's signature.

message: Existing tests only cover EventSchema. CreateEventSchema (with future-date validation) has no test coverage.
suggestion: Add a test block for CreateEventSchema covering valid future dates, rejected past dates, and the virtual-event-requires-link refiner.

message: The @deprecated JSDoc includes internal commentary ('Field name is a typo'), revealing implementation history to API consumers.
suggestion: Simplify to: /** @deprecated Use whyVolunteer instead. Will be removed in a future API version. */

message: whyVolunteer is accepted in the Zod schema and controller but has no Prisma schema field — it is stored in the deprecated whyVoluntary column. This prevents independent persistence for a future column rename migration.
suggestion: Add a whyVolunteer field to the User model in Prisma schema, or document that whyVolunteer is an alias for whyVoluntary.

message: Inconsistent import style: events.routes.ts and auth.routes.ts use direct relative imports while events.service.ts and 13+ other modules use the @/shared barrel import.
suggestion: Standardize on either barrel imports everywhere or direct imports everywhere, ideally in a follow-up PR.

message: Badge engine still reads totalHours from VolunteerProfile. After this PR, the leaderboard (User.totalHours) and badges (VolunteerProfile.totalHours) will report different values for the same user.
suggestion: Decide which field is canonical. If User.totalHours becomes the source of truth, migrate all reads to it and deprecate VolunteerProfile.totalHours.
